edges.description: Loss of the neuronal DST-a isoforms degenerates sympathetic and visceral afferent neurons as well as the dorsal root ganglion population. Drawn from the gene lesion directly rather than through the sensory-neuron cytoskeletal node, because the cited experiment inactivates Dst across peripheral neurons and reports both populations degenerating.

edges.description: Drawn so the autophagy arm descends from the same cytoskeletal lesion as its three siblings rather than floating as a root. Marked with known intermediates because the dependence of autophagosome transport on the microtubule network is the mechanism, and because which arm initiates degeneration is recorded as unresolved in the accompanying knowledge gap; this edge asserts shared origin, not primacy.

edges.description: The arrhythmia is neurogenic. It occurs without protein aggregate cardiomyopathy, and is reproduced by inactivating Dst in sensory neurons alone.
Reproduces the cytoskeletal disorganisation and sensory neuron degeneration of the human disease from loss of the orthologous gene.
edges.limitations: The mouse alleles are not the human alleles, and the human severity spectrum is driven by compound heterozygous combinations that the two mouse alleles do not span. The mouse also does not model the arthrogryposis of the severe human presentation.

edges.description: The autophagy defect was demonstrated in this allele: autophagosomes accumulate, flux is impaired, and substrates are not turned over.
edges.limitations: Autophagic flux was assayed in mouse sensory neurons; no equivalent measurement exists in human HSAN-VI tissue, so the human relevance of this arm is inferred from the shared gene rather than demonstrated.

edges.description: Models the isoform-selective loss that underlies the milder human phenotype, sparing DST-A3 as the milder human genotypes spare isoforms.
edges.limitations: Retained DST-A3 makes this allele a model of partial isoform loss rather than of the biallelic null state, so it under-represents the severe human presentation.

edges.description: Reproduces degeneration of sensory and sympathetic ganglionic neurons and the resulting arrhythmia, with the cell-type restriction that makes the causal attribution possible.
edges.limitations: The arrhythmia was most prominent under isoflurane anaesthesia, so the unanaesthetised human relevance of the magnitude is uncertain even though the mechanism is well localised.

edges.description: Schwann-cell-restricted loss gives late-onset neuropathy and sensory ataxia with sensory neurons largely intact, so it separates a glial contribution from the neuron-intrinsic disease.
edges.limitations: Dst expression was preserved in most dorsal root ganglion sensory neurons in this model, so it does not reproduce the neuron-intrinsic degeneration that drives the human disease and cannot stand in for it.

nodes.description: A conditional model that restricts Dst loss to peripheral neurons and asks whether the cardiac phenotype is neurogenic. It is the model that excludes a cardiomyopathic explanation for the arrhythmia.

evidence.reference_title: Rare autosomal recessive hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy type VI in a Pakistani family caused by a novel DST variant.
evidence.snippet: HSAN-VI (OMIM: 614653) is an autosomal recessive subtype which manifests severe pain insensitivity, neonatal hypotonia, respiratory and feeding difficulties, lack of psychomotor development and autonomic abnormalities.

evidence.reference_title: Rare autosomal recessive hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy type VI in a Pakistani family caused by a novel DST variant.
evidence.snippet: The most common symptoms occurring in 40% or more cases are pain insensitivity 82.3% (14/17), joint deformities 70.5% (12/17), skin ulcer 52.9% (9/17), respiratory insufficiency 41.1% (7/17), hypotonia 41.1% (7/17), feeding difficulty 41.1% (7/17), dysphagia 41.1% (7/17) and alacrima 41.1% (7/17).

nodes.description: Cardiac rhythm disturbance of neurogenic origin. The animal work shows it arises from disrupted visceral afferent circuits and not from a primary cardiomyopathy, which matters for how it should be monitored and treated.

evidence.reference_title: Disruption of afferent neural circuits leads to arrhythmia in the animal model of hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy 6.
evidence.snippet: These findings suggest that arrhythmias caused by Dst mutations arise from the disruption of visceral afferent circuits, and that these neural circuits could be potential therapeutic targets for visceral dysfunction in HSAN-VI.

evidence.reference_title: Rare autosomal recessive hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy type VI in a Pakistani family caused by a novel DST variant.
evidence.snippet: The clinical manifestations exhibited from birth include hypotonia, respiratory difficulty, absent deep tendon reflexes, autonomic instability involving tachy- or brady-arrhythmia, blood pressure fluctuations and recurrent episodes of hyperpyrexia of unknown origin

nodes.description: Degeneration extends to sympathetic ganglionic neurons and visceral afferent circuits, producing the dysautonomia. The mouse work localises the cardiac phenotype specifically to afferent circuit disruption rather than to any cardiomyopathy, which is a genuinely informative negative.

evidence.reference_title: Hereditary sensory autonomic neuropathy caused by a mutation in dystonin.
evidence.snippet: In 4 infants with a new lethal autonomic sensory neuropathy with clinical features similar to familial dysautonomia as well as contractures, we identified a deleterious mutation in the DST gene, using homozygosity mapping followed by exome sequencing.

evidence.reference_title: Hereditary sensory autonomic neuropathy caused by a mutation in dystonin.
evidence.snippet: DST encodes dystonin, a cytoskeleton linker protein, and the mutation results in an unstable transcript.

evidence.reference_title: Recessive mutations in the neuronal isoforms of DST, encoding dystonin, lead to abnormal actin cytoskeleton organization and HSAN type VI.
evidence.snippet: Here, we report novel biallelic mutations in the DST gene encoding dystonin, a large cytolinker protein of the plakin family, in an adult form of HSAN type VI.

evidence.reference_title: A possible cellular mechanism of neuronal loss in the dorsal root ganglia of Dystonia musculorum (dt) mice.
evidence.snippet: The active caspase-3 activity was observed in the dt neuron with massive accumulation of alpha-internexin.

nodes.description: The severe dystonia musculorum allele, disrupting all three neuronal isoforms. It is the model behind most of the transport, ER-stress and autophagy results, and its severity relative to the Tg4 allele is what established the isoform-dosage rule.
The milder allele, which spares DST-A3. It is the model that carries the negative result: it degenerates without microtubule instability, which is why instability cannot be the initiating lesion.

Dorsal root ganglion neurons mount an ER stress response, with altered ER chaperone expression, at a stage before limb incoordination begins. The timing is the argument: this is not a late consequence of a dying cell.

evidence.reference_title: Dystonin/Bpag1 is a necessary endoplasmic reticulum/nuclear envelope protein in sensory neurons.
evidence.snippet: Abnormalities include alterations in endoplasmic reticulum (ER) chaperone protein expression, indicative of an ER stress response.

evidence.reference_title: Dystonin/Bpag1 is a necessary endoplasmic reticulum/nuclear envelope protein in sensory neurons.
evidence.snippet: In the present study, we demonstrate perikaryal defects in dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons at stages preceding the onset of loss of limb coordination in dt mice.

nodes.description: Without the cytolinker the actin, neurofilament and microtubule networks are no longer tethered to one another. In the mouse this shows as perturbed neurofilament and microtubule organisation in axons and as mislocalisation and aggregation of alpha-internexin, whose interaction with dystonin appears to be part of what holds the neurofilament network in place.

nodes.description: Tests whether the neuropathy requires neuronal Dst loss or can arise from the Schwann cell. It produces a late-onset neuropathy, so glial loss contributes but does not reproduce the neonatal disease.

Ataxia from loss of proprioceptive afferents rather than from cerebellar disease. Prominent in the mouse. No cited human source names ataxia: it is absent from the 17-patient frequency table and from the founding gene-discovery report, so this phenotype rests on model-organism evidence and is recorded as such rather than being asserted as an established human finding.

evidence.reference_title: Disruption of dystonin in Schwann cells results in late-onset neuropathy and sensory ataxia.
evidence.snippet: Dystonin (Dst) is a causative gene for Dystonia musculorum (dt) mice, which is an inherited disorder exhibiting dystonia-like movement and ataxia with sensory degeneration.

nodes.description: There is no disease-modifying therapy. Management is airway and respiratory support, nutritional support, corneal protection for alacrima, wound and ulcer prevention in insensate limbs, and autonomic monitoring including cardiac rhythm.

evidence.reference_title: Rare autosomal recessive hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy type VI in a Pakistani family caused by a novel DST variant.
evidence.snippet: Effective care often involves a multidisciplinary team including a neurologist, geneticist, ophthalmologist and surgeon to manage affected individuals.

evidence.reference_title: Rare autosomal recessive hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy type VI in a Pakistani family caused by a novel DST variant.
evidence.snippet: Careful monitoring of high-friction areas, especially palms and soles, is crucial to detect trauma, prevent ulceration and subsequent joint deformities.
